skill.name: lint-typecheck
skill.description: Runs ESLint and TypeScript checks for a frontend workspace, reports file-level errors, and requests confirmation before applying automatic lint fixes.
skill.summary: Check frontend lint and TypeScript errors before committing changes.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: All five findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, not shell backtick execution. The fixed project-local checks do not expose a command injection path, and automatic lint fixes require user confirmation. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Offer to fix auto-fixable ESLint issues: `npm run lint -- --fix`

finding_verdicts.reason: The detected text is an opening Markdown fence for a Bash example, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The enclosed lint command uses fixed arguments.
This text is the closing Markdown fence for the lint example. It does not execute a command or interpolate input.
The detected text is an opening Markdown fence for the TypeScript example, not an execution construct. The enclosed type-check command uses fixed arguments.
This text is the closing Markdown fence for the TypeScript example. It has no executable behavior.
The backticks apply inline Markdown formatting to a fixed ESLint command, not shell substitution. The guardrails require user confirmation before applying fixes.

content.value_statement: Frontend changes can hide lint violations and type errors. This skill runs ESLint and TypeScript checks, then reports actionable results before any fixes.
actual_capabilities: Runs the configured npm lint script from the frontend directory.
Runs the TypeScript build checker without emitting compiled files.
Lists discovered errors with their source file locations.
Separates lint warnings, lint errors, and type errors in the summary.
Offers automatic ESLint fixes only after user confirmation.
limitations: Assumes the project has a frontend directory and the required npm tooling.
Does not install dependencies or create missing lint and TypeScript configuration.
Does not modify TypeScript configuration to suppress errors.
Automatic changes are limited to ESLint fixes and require confirmation.

use_cases.title: Check Changes Before Commit
use_cases.description: Find lint and type failures in frontend changes before they enter version control.

use_cases.title: Review Code Quality
use_cases.description: Collect file-level validation results before reviewing a frontend pull request.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Failed Validation
use_cases.description: Reproduce lint and TypeScript failures locally and summarize the reported causes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Frontend Lint
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint on the frontend and report every warning and error with its file location.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a quick lint check.

prompt_templates.title: Check TypeScript Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Check frontend TypeScript types without emitting files. Group failures by file and explain each reported mismatch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when type safety is the main concern.

prompt_templates.title: Run Complete Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run both frontend lint and TypeScript checks. Summarize warning, lint error, and type error counts before proposing changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before committing a completed frontend change.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose and Fix Lint
prompt_templates.prompt: Run both checks and diagnose root causes. Ask before applying only automatic ESLint fixes, then rerun validation after approved changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for controlled remediation after a broad validation pass.

output: Lint completed with two warnings and one error.
Each issue is listed with its source file and location.

output_examples.input: Check the frontend for TypeScript errors.
output: Type checking completed without generating compiled files.
Three type mismatches were found and grouped by source file.
Each mismatch includes a concise explanation.

best_practices: Run both checks before committing important frontend changes.
Review the complete issue list before selecting any remediation.
Approve automatic lint fixes only after checking their expected scope.
anti_patterns: Do not apply automatic fixes without explicit user confirmation.
Do not suppress TypeScript errors by changing configuration.
Do not omit warnings or combine distinct error counts.

faq.question: What checks does this skill run?
faq.answer: It runs the configured frontend ESLint script and a TypeScript build check without emitting files.

faq.question: Does it change source files?
faq.answer: Initial checks are read-only. It can apply automatic ESLint fixes only after user confirmation.

faq.question: Does TypeScript create compiled output?
faq.answer: No. The TypeScript check uses the no-emit option.

faq.question: What project structure does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a frontend directory with npm tooling, a lint script, and TypeScript configuration.

faq.question: Can it fix TypeScript errors automatically?
faq.answer: No automatic TypeScript repair is promised. The skill identifies reported type mismatches for review.

faq.question: How are results reported?
faq.answer: Results include file locations and separate totals for lint warnings, lint errors, and type errors.
